Genes, Populations, & Evolution
¨A populationis all the members of a single species occupying a particular area at the same time.
¨Diversity exists among members of a population.
¨Population genetics is the study of this diversity in terms of allele differences.
¤Evaluates the diversity of a population by studying genotype and phenotype frequencies over time
¨In the 1930s, population geneticists began to describe variations in a population in terms of alleles
¨Microevolution pertains to evolutionary changes within a population.
¤Various alleles at all the gene loci in all individuals make up the gene pool of the population.
¤The gene pool of a population can be described in terms of:
  nGenotype frequencies
  nAllele frequencies
explanation: This page introduces the foundation of population genetics. A population is defined as all the members of a single species occupying a particular area at the same time. Genetic diversity is inherent in populations, and population genetics is the scientific study of this diversity in terms of allele differences, evaluating changes in genotype and phenotype frequencies over time. In the 1930s, geneticists began describing these population variations specifically using alleles. Microevolution refers to evolutionary changes that occur within a population. The gene pool is the collection of all the alleles at all gene loci across all individuals in that population, and it can be quantitatively described using genotype frequencies and allele frequencies.

questions.q: What is the definition of a population in the context of genetics and evolution?
opts: All the different species living in a particular area at different times
All members of a single species occupying a particular area at the same time
A group of organisms that are genetically identical
The total number of genes in a particular habitat
questions.exp: The notes define a population as 'all the members of a single species occupying a particular area at the same time.'

questions.q: What makes up the gene pool of a population?
opts: The geographic boundaries that isolate a species
The somatic cells that undergo mitosis
Various alleles at all the gene loci in all individuals of the population
The external physical traits determined by environmental selection pressures
questions.exp: The gene pool consists of the collection of all the various alleles at all the gene loci across all the individuals in a population.
